item.title: About
item.dc:creator: anuradhawick
item.content:encoded:
Hi! I am Anuradha 😃

I am currently an Engineer at AML3D, an ex-CSIRO and I got my PhD from the Australian National University (ANU), Australia. My area of research is Bioinformatics and Computational Biology. I like to do exploratory genomics research, statistical analysis, and modelling machine learning methods. But of them all, I love coding 😃.

Researcher profile at Google Scholar 🎓

📄 My PhD thesis is here 🎓

📄 My CV is available here 💻 Code for it is here

Contact Details 📱

  • Email - personal: info@anuradhawick.com
  • LinkedIn: anuradhawick
  • BlueSky: @anuradhawick.bsky.social

I Love Research 🔬

I love doing research that is usually computationally challenging and requires novel thinking. I am an enthusiastic blogger and write about new things I learn as I do my research. Check my blog here!

I am a hobbyist DIY’er

On my free time I like to mess around with Jetson Nano, Raspberry Pi and other SOCs like Onion Omega, ESP and Arduino. ⚡️🔋

I also love doing self defined machine learning projects and compute optimisation tasks on CUDA. You’ll find most of them in my GitHub or as Gists. 👨‍💻🧠

Education 👨🏽‍🎓

  • Currently an engineer at CSIRO, the national Australian research agency. I design and develop population scale systems for genomics and healthcare.
  • I got my PhD from ANU, School of Computing, College of Engineering and Computer Science, Australia. I spent 3.5 years in the Aussie capital, Canberra.
  • I obtained my BSc (Hons) in Computer Science and Engineering from the University of Moratuwa, Sri Lanka. I was able to secure a GPA of 4+ (out of 4.2) along with several other non-academic achievements.
  • I was ranked 68th all-island (4th in the entire district) in my Advanced Level examination in the physical sciences stream.

From Sri Lanka 🇱🇰 and Found Home in Australia 🇦🇺

I Love to Travel 🏝

My hometown is located in Gampaha District a small non-urban town. I grew up playing on grass and mud. I cherish those days I was playing with my brother and kids from the neighbourhood. A simple village life that wasn’t rural and definitely wasn’t urban. Even to date, I am inspired by simple livelihoods that leave plenty of time to free thought and creativity.

Now that my wife and I are in Australia, we roam around the continent whenever we have a chance.

item.title: Home
item.dc:creator: anuradhawick
item.content:encoded:
G'day!

I work as an solutions architect for building bioinformatics products at CSIRO, Australia's National Science Agency. Have a look at our research group, Transformational Bioinformatics Group.

I did my PhD at the Australian National University. My thesis title was "Models and algorithms for metagenomics binning and plasmid classification". I love reading algorithms, tinkering on SBCs, travelling and gaming (PC/XBOX/PS). On holidays I am either driving or cooking!

In any case, happy to connect connect via LinkedIn as a fellow researcher, DIY'er, programming geek, or as a fellow human being! :-)

Professionally, I am a research software engineer, developing cloud-first bioinformatics software. I also work in computational biology and bioinformatics, applying computational/machine learning methods in the domain of genomics.

The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing.
Walt Disney

Code commit format

Suggest a precise and point form commit message based on the following diff. Do not use markdown syntax in your response.

The commit message should have description with a short title that follows conventional commit message format like <type>: <description>.

Examples:
- FIX: add 403 forbidden error cases
- FEAT: generate commit messages from changes
- DEV: implemented feature to handle users
- DOCS: added code comments/modified readme 

If necessary, follow with an explanatory body providing insight into the nature of the changes, the reasoning behind them, and any significant consequences or considerations arising from them.

item.title: Software
item.dc:creator: anuradhawick
item.content:encoded:
Signature Tools

Clipper

Clipper is a versatile clipboard management and note-taking application designed specifically for developers. It runs on Mac and Linux, leveraging the Tauri framework for a lightweight and secure experience. With Clipper, accessing your clipboard history and jotting down notes becomes seamless and integrated into your development workflow.

https://github.com/anuradhawick/clipper

Kmertools

kmertools is a k-mer based feature extraction tool designed to support metagenomics and other bioinformatics analytics.

https://anaconda.org/bioconda/kmertools

https://github.com/anuradhawick/kmertools

TypeFaster

Simple angular webapp to help to top your typing game

https://typefaster.anuradhawick.com

https://github.com/anuradhawick/typefaster

Other Tools

Seq2Vec

Seq2Vec is a software to convert metagenomics long reads (or contigs) into oligo-nucleotide frequency vectors. The main motivation of the tool is to be fast and robust. Seq2Vec uses memory mapped output files to operate in a highly parallel manner. Give it a go https://github.com/anuradhawick/seq2vec.

Seq2CovVec

This more or less does the same of Seq2Vec. However, this tool generate coverage vectors for long reads (or contigs). This tools implements the k-mer coverage histogram explained in MetaBCC-LR. Give it a go https://github.com/anuradhawick/seq2covvec.

Metagenomics and plasmid recovery

My PhD study was on developing efficient algorithms and models for metagenomics binning and plasmid recovery. Following are the software that I developed during my study.

  • MetaBCC-LR - my first binning tool. Introduced the concept of k-mer coverage histogram. Uses TSNE for dimension reduction and DBSCAN for clustering. Try it https://github.com/metagentools/MetaBCC-LR.
  • LRBinner - one disadvantage of MetaBCC-LR was having to use coverage and composition in two steps. Resolved that using an auto-encoder to combine the two features. Also developed a new clustering algorithm. Try it https://github.com/anuradhawick/lrbinner.
  • OBLR - this tool brought in read-overlap graph to binning long reads. UMAP detect clusters and GraphSAGE perform labelling. Perform probabilistic sampling to address the issue of variable cluster sizes. Implemented using the CUDA RAPIDS library. Try it https://github.com/anuradhawick/oblr.

Computer Vision

In computer vision, training of an object detector is challenging due to limited training data. However, Object Annotation maker I created would help someone to bootstrap images based on a target image and a set of backgrounds. Try it https://github.com/anuradhawick/Object-Annotation-Maker.

Serverless Boilerplate

Serverless computing is very popular in web service development and rapid prototyping. I have made this simplistic boilerplate to get you started. I am using it myself in https://vinyl.lk. Try it https://github.com/anuradhawick/aws-lambda-serverless-boilerplate.

CUDA Scripts

CUDA programming in C++ is challenging. Have a look at my simple k-mer counter. I made this for a presentation at work. Bits and pieces may be re-usable. Give it a peek https://github.com/anuradhawick/CUDA-k-mer-counting.

Also https://github.com/anuradhawick/GPU-Optimized-Algorithms to see how you can write CUDA code for some algorithms.

And this https://github.com/anuradhawick/GPU-Optimized-Biological-Data-Analysis to see how I have implemented the Needleman-Wunsch algorithm (NW algorithm) in bioinformatics.

item.dc:creator: anuradhawick
item.content:encoded:
Rust AWS Lambda Template

This repository contains a Rust-based AWS Lambda function, managed using the cargo-lambda tool and deployed via Terraform.

https://github.com/anuradhawick/rs_template

Template Web Server

A template for deploying a web site to AWS using terraform. Example contains an angular web app but it could be anything. Example has two lambdas for you to get started, one using pure python and another that uses docker to deploy a python backend.

https://github.com/anuradhawick/tf_template
